verdicts.reason: A puts the CTA at the very top left, before the headline, and clips it against a dark band fragment. The oversized logo dominates the canvas, the headline is tiny and about the same size as the body copy, the body copy runs right to the edges, and 'Ships late June' is set larger than the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. B keeps the right reading order (logo, headline, body, CTA, legal) and the CTA has some presence. But the logo is still oversized, the dark band is a stray partial strip in the top right, the headline is small and cramped, and the body and legal text are close to illegible.
